title: Load the billing overview in one statement

blocks.text: The billing overview lists every invoice with its lines. It loads them with `loadAllSlowly()`, and the database team has traced one overview to 341 statements. The numbers are right; the round trips are the problem.

Write `loadAll()` in `src/main/java/practice/InvoiceRepository.java`. It returns what `loadAllSlowly()` returns: every invoice in id order, including invoices that have no lines yet, each one once, with its lines in line-number order. It may send the database only one statement, however many invoices there are. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests run the repository against H2 in memory through a connection that counts the statements it executes.

cases.says: every invoice comes back in id order with its customer and its line
the whole overview, whatever the number of invoices, is loaded by one executed statement
an invoice that has no lines yet is still in the overview
an invoice with several lines appears once, holding all of them in line order
an invoice without lines has an empty list, not a line made of the join's empty columns

origin.section: A Lazy Association Costs One Query per Parent Unless the Query Fetches It

concepts: join fetch is an inner join, so a parent with no children is not returned; left join fetch keeps it.
Reading a lazy collection on each parent a query returned runs one more statement per parent; a fetch join loads parents and children in one statement.
